claims.text: A data-driven machine-learning workflow can optimize processing conditions in non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning-guided processing can tune phase distribution and grain-boundary characteristics.
The resulting microstructural tuning will enhance magnetic performance.
The resulting microstructural tuning will enhance magnetocaloric performance in low-dimensional HEAs.
The proposed starting materials are non-equiatomic HEAs in an as-cast or as-synthesized state and with low-dimensional geometry.
The workflow will systematically vary heat-treatment profiles, thickness reduction, and consolidation routes.
Changes in processing can modify HEA phase constituents and grain size.
Changes in processing can modify magnetic-domain structures in the target HEAs.
A machine-learning model can identify correlations between processing variables and microstructural attributes in these HEAs.
Microstructural or phase attributes affect magnetic ordering in HEAs.
Processing-controlled microstructural attributes govern magnetic entropy changes under applied magnetic fields.
Machine-learning-optimized microstructures will produce a larger magnetic entropy change than conventionally processed samples.
Machine-learning-guided processing will produce more desirable ferromagnetic transition temperatures than conventional processing.
The effectiveness of the proposed workflow may depend on the alloy system and on whether processing parameters remain within the explored range.
X-ray diffraction can be used for phase identification and electron microscopy for microstructural characterization in HEAs.
The magnitude of any magnetic or magnetocaloric enhancement remains uncertain and requires experimental validation.
